key_insight: Bulk second-gradient elasticity supports minimizer existence for broadly admissible surface energies while introducing a length scale that delays elastocapillary beading and favors longer wavelengths.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps predict how intrinsic material length scales affect instability onset and beaded shapes in stretched soft cylinders with energetic surfaces.
method: Prove minimizer existence under bulk coercivity and second-gradient convexity assumptions.
Derive a finite-strain, small-on-large incremental formulation for cylinder stability.
Implement C1-continuous isogeometric analysis in OOFEM and trace post-bifurcation branches using arc-length continuation.
evidence_signal: Finite-cylinder simulations closely match analytical onset stretches; selected post-bifurcation branches show supercritical beading at small second-gradient moduli and subcritical thick–thin segmentation at larger moduli.
watch_item: The reported trends concern the cylinder configurations and parameters studied, and implementation requires C1-continuous discretization.
paper_title: Finite-strain second-gradient elasticity with an energetic surface: existence of minimizers, incremental theory and elastocapillary beading
